window_nonempty_proof.positivity_reason: r=sqrt(3)>1, so (r-1)^4>0 and 8*r*(1+r^2)>0; hence the log2 argument is >1
window_nonempty_proof.consequence: there exists beta strictly between A(tau) and C(tau)

secondary_parameters.L0: choose an integer L0>=4 large enough for eta(L)<delta and the source finite-size error inequality for every L>=L0
secondary_parameters.existence: strict positivity beta-A(tau)>0 and delta<(beta-A(tau))/4 imply beta-A(tau)-2*delta>(beta-A(tau))/2>0, so such s exists

fixed_forbidden_graph.layers: take disjoint finite layers V0,...,Vs with |V0|=L0 and Vi=choose(Vi-1,2) for 1<=i<=s
fixed_forbidden_graph.vertices: a vertex in Vi for i>=1 is an unordered pair {a,b} of distinct vertices of V(i-1)
fixed_forbidden_graph.edges: join each child {a,b} in Vi to exactly its two parents a,b in V(i-1)
fixed_forbidden_graph.finite: L0 and s are fixed finite integers; recursive finite pair formation therefore gives a fixed finite graph H

connected.proof: Every two distinct vertices of V0 share a child in V1, so V0 lies in one connected component. Every vertex in Vi for i>=1 has parent edges descending to V0, hence all layers lie in that component.

bipartite.proof: Every edge joins consecutive layers. Color a vertex by the parity of its layer index; every edge changes parity.
bipartite.color_classes: union of even-index layers versus union of odd-index layers

two_degenerate.proof: Order vertices by decreasing layer index. When a vertex of Vi, i>=1, is considered, all children in V(i+1) have already been removed and only its two parents can remain. Vertices of V0 are considered last. Thus every nonempty induced remainder has a vertex of degree at most 2.
two_degenerate.scope: establishes 2-degeneracy; no coloring-side maximum-degree property is used

sampled_host.base_host: two disjoint copies U_L,U_R; join opposite-side words when Hamming distance is at most k
sampled_host.random_host: retain each vertex independently with probability p and take the induced bipartite subgraph G_m

source_dependencies: Chapter 10 Lemma 5.1: entropy inequality for a parent pair and child
Chapter 10 Lemma 5.2: finite-array approximation of the entropy inequality
Chapter 10 Lemma 7.1: with probability at least 1-2*s*2^(-m), no retained transition array has conditional entropy E(u,z)<=beta-delta
exclusion_argument.embedding_setup: Assume the Lemma 7.1 event and an embedding iota:H->G_m. Because H is connected and bipartite, consecutive layers occupy opposite host sides.
exclusion_argument.entropy_potential: Phi_i=(1/m)*sum_j h((1/L_i)*sum_{z in iota(V_i)} z(j)); therefore 0<=Phi_i<=1
exclusion_argument.transition_lower_bound: Lemma 7.1 gives E_i>beta-delta for each layer transition
exclusion_argument.transition_upper_bound: Lemma 5.2 plus the Hamming-radius condition gives E_i<=A(tau)+(Phi_i-Phi_(i-1))/2+eta(L_(i-1))
exclusion_argument.finite_size_control: the choice of L0 and recursive growth L_i>=L0 makes eta(L_(i-1))<delta and absorbs the finite collision/profile term used in the source
exclusion_argument.increment: combining the lower and upper bounds gives Phi_i-Phi_(i-1)>2*(beta-A(tau)-2*delta)
exclusion_argument.conclusion: P(H subseteq G_m)<=2*s*2^(-m)=o(1), so G_m is H-free with probability 1-o(1)
exclusion_argument.independent_assessment: The dependency chain and inequality directions were reconstructed independently. This evidence does not claim a new formal proof of Lemmas 5.1, 5.2, or 7.1; their source proofs remain part of the admitted theorem proof body.

host_size_and_edge_count.simultaneous_positive_probability: The H-free event and both concentration events each have probability 1-o(1), so for all sufficiently large m an H-free realization satisfies both size bounds.

extremal_bridge.padding_reason: an H-free realization has W_m<=3*p*Q<=N_m vertices; add isolated vertices to reach N_m without adding edges or creating H
extremal_bridge.strict_gain: C(tau)-beta>0 and 1-beta>0, so the exponent ratio is strictly greater than 3/2
extremal_bridge.subsequence_consequence: for all sufficiently large m, ex(N_m,H)>=N_m^(3/2+epsilon) after absorbing fixed/subexponential factors into the strict exponent slack
extremal_bridge.all_n_padding: for every sufficiently large n choose m with N_m<=n<N_(m+1)<=2*N_m; pad an H-free N_m-vertex graph with isolated vertices to n vertices
extremal_bridge.final_bound: ex(n,H)>=c*n^(3/2+epsilon) for all sufficiently large n
extremal_bridge.interpretation: An H-free graph on n vertices with at least c*n^(3/2+epsilon) edges is exactly a lower-bound witness for the extremal number ex(n,H).

refutation_bridge.conjectured_r2_bound: every fixed bipartite 2-degenerate H has ex(n,H)=O(n^(3/2))
refutation_bridge.source_lower_bound: for the fixed H above, ex(n,H)>=c*n^(3/2+epsilon) eventually with c,epsilon>0
refutation_bridge.contradiction: n^epsilon is unbounded, so no fixed O(n^(3/2)) constant can dominate c*n^(3/2+epsilon) for all sufficiently large n
